title: American bands in Paris and seeing Armstrong at Bricktop's
summary: Whiteman, Glenn Miller and others visited; Armstrong was glad to see him, having played with him in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Were many American jazz bands over in Paris those years you were there? Did they come over all the time?
Yeah, they used to come over the big bands. Like, well, just before I left there, Glenn Miller.
But back in the olden days, Paul Whiteman. And this was this great dance band, you know. Now, Bob Begarden, that's not it.
Ellington, I guess, he was over there too, wasn't he?
No, Ellington wasn't there the whole time I was there. No. But I used to come back, when I come back, and...
Did you see Armstrong over there? Yes, he sent for me.

I was in bed when he was in his friendship over there. He was at Brick Tops. Gee, he was glad to see me, and I was glad to see him, because I used to play with him, you know, yeah. Over here? At Dreamland 35, or 40, or 8.
